facts.raw_span: involuntary movements of her left upper and lower limbs for more than 10 days
a history of untreated type 2 diabetes mellitus
slow response, reduced muscle strength, and positive tendon reflexes in her left limbs
Continuous, irregular involuntary movements of variable amplitude were observed in the left arm and leg
a blood glucose level of 8.59 mmol/L
a hemoglobin A1c of 7.43%
all other laboratory values within normal limits
Noncontrast CT of the head showed slightly increased density in the bilateral striatal regions
without evidence of acute infarction
high-signal intensity on T1-weighted images in the bilateral basal ganglia

concepts.why: The patient's involuntary movements of her left upper and lower limbs, along with the high-signal intensity on T1-weighted images in the bilateral basal ganglia, are consistent with hemichorea.
The patient's history of untreated type 2 diabetes mellitus, along with her abnormal glucose levels, suggests a possible link to diabetic chorea.
The patient's noncontrast CT and brain MRI results showing abnormalities in the bilateral basal ganglia suggest a basal ganglia disease.
The patient's involuntary movements, along with her neurological examination abnormalities, are consistent with dyskinesia.
It explains the absence of acute infarction in the brain imaging of a patient with high blood glucose levels.
